title: How many fractions lie between zero and one?
description: The number line from zero to one is cut into more and more equal parts. Each cut gives a new mark between zero and one, and the board shows that the list of fractions can always be made longer and never has a last one.
teaching_notes: One idea: cutting the unit into more equal parts always gives new, smaller fractions between zero and one. Watch for students who think there is a last fraction before zero.

source: Figure it Out Q3 (section 7.4), Math Talk
video_script.why: A learner sees that cutting the unit into more equal parts keeps giving new fractions between zero and one.
video_script.substitution: the book's number line from 0 to 1 cut into more and more equal parts
video_script.anchor: a number line from 0 to 1 cut into more and more equal parts
video_script.payoff_line: There are infinitely many fractions between zero and one

final_answer.spoken: infinitely many, there is no end to them

video_script.fraction_reading: one half, one third, one fourth, one fifth, one hundredth, one thousandth
never_show: a fixed count of fractions between 0 and 1
maths_rules: cut 0 to 1 into 2, 3, 4, 5 equal parts: the first marks are 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/5, all between 0 and 1
cut into 100 or 1000 equal parts: 1/100 and 1/1000 are also between 0 and 1
the bottom number can always be made bigger, so the fractions never run out
video_script.design: One number line from zero to one that gets cut again and again. Each new cut adds a mark between zero and one.

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>There are infinitely many fractions between zero and one.
